risks.reasoning: The latest formal interim cash-flow period shows positive net cash generated from operating activities. Under Protocol v1.1.1, non-negative operating cash flow is not operating cash burn, so monthly operating cash burn and cash runway are null.
All disclosed comparable annual and latest interim periods are profitable. There are zero comparable loss periods, so neither the two-period medium trigger nor the three-period high trigger is met.

For the latest comparable interim period, total net revenues declined from USD 1,071,777 thousand to USD 986,366 thousand, a year-on-year decrease of about 7.97%. This is below 0% but above -20%, meeting the frozen medium threshold.

The accountants' report states that no customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated net revenues in FY2018-FY2020. Preserving the strict bound gives each customer <10%, hence the top five customers are <50%, which excludes both frozen medium and high concentration thresholds.

The Business section states that the five largest suppliers accounted for less than 8% of total purchases in each year of the Track Record Period. This strict top-five bound is far below both frozen supplier-concentration thresholds.

calculation_inputs.period: each year of the Track Record Period

risks.reasoning: The disclosed redeemable preferred-share rights related to New Oriental Holdings, a subsidiary, not the listed issuer's ordinary shares. New Oriental Holdings completed its qualified IPO in March 2019; the related mezzanine equity was reclassified, and the preferred shares were subject to automatic conversion immediately before a qualified IPO. The disclosed special redemption rights were therefore terminated rather than effective or restorable at the listing date.

A putative securities class action against the company and its CEO remained pending: a motion for preliminary approval of a class settlement was awaiting court review and the prospectus states the case was still ongoing. The prospectus expressly cross-references the risk that this pending case could have a material adverse effect. This meets the frozen material-pending-matter trigger; medium is the protocol's provisional candidate severity.

The group is a mature commercial education-services business with broad established offerings, approximately 10.6 million student enrollments in K-12 tutoring/test-preparation and other courses in FY2020, and USD 3.58 billion of total net revenues. The core business is already commercialized, so the precommercial-product candidate condition is not met.

evidence.evidence_reason: The latest interim balance sheet provides the formal period-end cash and cash equivalents amount used as the standard cash input.
The latest three-month period has positive operating cash flow of USD391,598 thousand, which directly establishes that there is no operating cash burn under the protocol.
The cash-flow statement provides the period-end combined cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash balance, allowing cross-check against the separately disclosed cash and restricted-cash components.
The audited accountants' report shows positive net income in each of FY2018, FY2019 and FY2020, establishing zero loss years across three comparable annual periods.
The latest comparable three-month periods are also profitable, confirming that the more recent interim period does not introduce a loss period.
This formal interim financial statement gives directly comparable total net revenues for the three months ended 31 August 2019 and 2020, from which the approximately 7.97% decline is calculated.
The audited annual figures cross-check that annual revenues grew through FY2020; the medium trigger arises specifically from the latest comparable interim decline.
